summary.text: In an April 2024 posture statement, General Eric M. Smith said the Marine Corps is leveraging AI, robotics, and commercial technology as part of the Department of Defense’s Replicator Initiative (s1), and he described Replicator as an opportunity to accelerate modernization if managed carefully (s2). In other posture statements, Smith described integrating AI with sensors and targeting systems to improve sensing and precision fires (s3), and moving to an increment that adds edge-based AI and electronic warfare capabilities (s4). In a May 2026 statement, Smith said Dynamis enables AI-powered decision advantage by integrating commercial technologies with Marine Corps warfighting functions (s5), and that MSS, used by over 4,900 Marines, reflects leveraging AI to shape decision-making and improve kill-chain capabilities (s6). In January 2025, Smith said the Marine Corps would not reorganize based on AI but would use available tools (s7); in May 2025 he described expanding AI-driven adaptive learning in education and training (s12, s13) and stated that there is always a human on the loop (s15).

Smith said the Marine Corps is leveraging AI, robotics, and commercial technology as part of the Department of Defense’s Replicator Initiative (s1), and he described Replicator as an opportunity to accelerate modernization if managed carefully (s2).

In other posture statements, Smith described integrating AI with sensors and targeting systems to improve sensing and precision fires (s3), and moving to an increment that adds edge-based AI and electronic warfare capabilities (s4).

In a May 2026 statement, Smith said Dynamis enables AI-powered decision advantage by integrating commercial technologies with Marine Corps warfighting functions (s5), and that MSS, used by over 4,900 Marines, reflects leveraging AI to shape decision-making and improve kill-chain capabilities (s6).

In January 2025, Smith said the Marine Corps would not reorganize based on AI but would use available tools (s7); in May 2025 he described expanding AI-driven adaptive learning in education and training (s12, s13) and stated that there is always a human on the loop (s15).

statements.text: The Marine Corps is actively engaged, participating, and, in some instances, leading efforts within the Department of Defense’s Replicator Initiative, which aims to field attritable autonomous systems at scale and in multiple domains. To accomplish this task, the Marine Corps is aggressively leveraging AI, robotics, and commercial technology.
